method.design: leave one report out, same party same day also removed

rows.quote: Tyndall was dangerous at midday, waist deep and fast
Continuous deep snow from Saddlerock Lake, the final ramp is a proper snow climb right now, crampons ideally
Axe mandatory in my opinion, saw someone self arrest for real
I was on spikes and wishing for an axe
Snow starts just past Loch Leven, continuous to the pass, but it is the gentle kind, spikes in the morning and bare boots after lunch
It is a wall of snow with a bergschrund looking crack near the top
Woods Creek ford was the scariest thing I have done on trail, waist deep, moving hard, we linked arms
Continuous snow from Ruby Lake, firm and pleasant at 6am
continuous but mellow, no traction used just careful steps in the morning crust
continuous snow to the top
Sawmill Creek crossing was knee high with a strong push at midday
Tyndall crossing thigh high at 5pm
There is a steep snow chute on the north side and people had cut steps into it
Boot pack all the way up the chute, firm at 5am, axe in hand but never needed it, spikes did the work
Continuous snow from Bishop Lake up
the snow got continuous and we only had trail runners
it was still waist deep at 8am
north side snowfield is going fast, boot path is deep and obvious, spikes for the first hour only
Continuous snow on the Lyell headwall side, moderate angle, good steps, spikes used morning only
The headwall chute is still full of snow and it is steep enough that a slide would hurt.
South side had a snow ramp with good steps
Bubbs down to mid calf
one 30 foot snow patch, no axe no spikes
Patchy snow in the last half mile, totally walkable, the little ones loved the snowfield glissade near the top.
Taboose Creek is running strong at the second crossing, knee high early
the famous snowfield is down to maybe 80 feet with a boot trench you could push a stroller through
The creek crossings were knee high at 8am
one tiny snow bank right at the pass that you walk around
the upper one was thigh high and fast at 2pm
snow is patchy at worst on every pass now
Palisade Creek crossing knee high
West side holds patchy snow in the trees, pass is clear
pass itself is clear, tiny patch on the west ramp you can avoid
Snow is down to maybe a mile total near the hut, sun cupped but flat. Trail runners fine all day.
Only a few snow patches left near the top and you can walk around all of them
The headwall is melted out to scree with one hard snow finger you cross in ten steps, kicked steps are in, no axe needed anymore
completely snow free top to bottom
Zero snow anywhere near the trail, the north side chute of legend is just blocky talus
Snow free both sides, the chute is dry, Tyndall Creek is ankle deep
Bone dry
